Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and current evidence. I’m using the fish-control-primitives skill because you explicitly required the structured transfer protocol, and the read-wake-visual-signals-first skill because this policy change requires inspecting both 3D rollout views before editing.

The workspace confirms this is a still-water, no-cylinder L64 task and prohibits running CFD locally. I’m now anchoring the visual comparison to scores, observations, metrics, diagnostics, inherited guidance, and the prefilled policy before proposing any architecture.

All four sampled candidates are true direct-uniform, zero-inflow, zero-cylinder captures at roughly 16T; their scalar spread is small and the tight 0.75L trigger makes terminal geometry more informative than raw score alone. I’m comparing the highest-score capture with the closest-threshold capture and will also use inherited misses as the failure contrast.

The inherited failure preserves propulsion and the same compact wake through the near pass, then continues left after crossing roughly 1.10L from the target; there is no collision, wake collapse, or numerical instability. The assigned parent’s angle-domain phase correction therefore worsened terminal geometry despite a healthy carrier. Following the required bookshelf protocol, I’m consulting mechanism-level primitives now; any transfer will be restricted to normalized body-frame state feedback.

The transferable mechanism is a redirect-to-cruise handoff: measured yaw response should release steering only after residual target geometry is also small. Here, successful crossings have body-frame lateral target offsets of `0.334–0.392L`, while inherited near misses have `0.760–0.890L`; response-only release and several phase-estimator variants all missed. I’ll record that diagnosis and the falsifiable corridor-gated handoff before touching the policy.

The notes and durable guidance now capture the bookshelf transfer and the negative evidence from all four failed phase/handoff variants. I’m applying only the corridor-conditioned release: it preserves the carrier, requests, prediction, mean bend, and posterior pulse, while preventing response feedback from prematurely reducing half-cycle steering outside the observed capture corridor.

The candidate remains non-empty and all new parameter references are defined by `target_policy_params()`. I’m now invoking the required non-CFD checks separately: semantic guidance change, Julia policy contract, then editable-boundary validation.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one parent. I’ll remove only that duplicate marker and rerun; this does not alter solver behavior or guidance evidence.

The boundary invocation used the lineage root instead of this Phase 2 workspace, so it compared the wrong `solver/` tree and reported the entire repository as forbidden. No files were deleted or changed. I’m rerunning the identical check from the required workspace root.

All three required checks now pass. I’m doing one additional lightweight symmetry and boundedness probe (still no CFD) because the new gate uses an absolute body-frame offset and should remain reflection-equivariant while respecting the ±30 acceleration bound.

The extra probe did not start—the execution wrapper reported a process-creation error rather than a policy assertion. I’m checking the workspace path and will rerun the small probe if the environment is intact.

The rerun passes reflection and boundedness, including extreme and NaN-fallback inputs. I’m performing a final file-level audit now so the handoff points to the exact candidate mechanism, provenance notes, and reusable lesson.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate: a corridor-gated redirect release in [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:172). Corrective yaw reduces half-cycle steering only after lateral target error enters the observed capture corridor.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) with visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:122) with an evidence-backed negative lesson covering four failed phase/handoff mechanisms.
- Removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:123) so the required checker could resolve the parent.

All required checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, editable boundary, reflection equivariance, finite fallbacks, and acceleration boundedness. CFD was intentionally not run.
